subject: Prod demo recap: target unit economics & surge guardrails
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Dunn <adunn@clearwave.ai>, procure@clearwave.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Prod demo recap: target unit economics & surge guardrails

Hi Alex / ClearWave procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning — appreciate the clear signals on where this will land from a usage and product perspective. Short recap + asks so we can turn this into a pilot proposal.

1) Observed / expected profile (from our call)
- Steady-state: ~2.2M tokens/month (text generation across user journeys).
- Campaign spikes: up to ~6M tokens/day during marketing pushes (~4x daily baseline for 24-48 hour windows).
- Typical latency requirement: p95 < 250ms for interactive flows; occasional async batches OK for reports.

2) Unit economics target (your note: procurement looking for $$$/1M tokens)
- You mentioned a target range around $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens depending on model family and SLA.
- For a pilot we usually propose a committed unit that balances cost predictability and burst flexibility. See proposed ranges below.

3) Burst / quota and overage framing (we heard you want predictable caps for finance)
- Baseline quota = committed monthly tokens (example: 2M).
- Burst buffer: we can offer an elastic burst pool that allows short-term spikes (configurable window) without immediate overage charges.
- Overage tiers apply if burst > allowance for the billing period; we can cap absolute spend for surprise protection if needed.

Proposed pilot (for internal discussion):
- Term: 3 months
- Committed: 2M tokens/month
- Committed unit price: $900 / 1M tokens
- Burst allowance: up to 25% of committed tokens/day for up to 2 hours/day, or 2x baseline for up to 48 hours per month (configurable)
- Overage pricing: $1,200 / 1M tokens up to 2x committed in a billing period; pay-as-you-go $1,600 / 1M beyond that
- One-time onboarding credit: 30% credit on usage for first 30 days (applies to committed + overage up to a cap)

Attached: redwood-pricing-template.xlsx (simple worksheet you can populate with your expected volumes) and SLA-summary.pdf.

Next steps / asks:
- Alex: can you confirm steady-state monthly token estimate and whether ClearWave wants an absolute up-front spend cap on overages?
- Procurement: ideal contract signature window and PO process?
- We'll draft a pilot quote and DocuSign-ready proposal once you confirm the numbers.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up with procurement as needed.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0119

Subject: Re: Prod demo recap: target unit economics & surge guardrails

Evelyn — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Steady-state looks right: ~2.2M tokens/month is our internal median estimate once the feature is GA.
- Spikes are a concern: marketing/promotions will generate ~5–6M tokens/day across a 24–48hr window, maybe 3–4 times per quarter. We need to make sure those spikes don't blow up cost predictability.
- Procurement preference: an overage cap we can set at the beginning of the quarter (e.g., max $12k/month in overages) so finance can model worst-case spend.

Question: will the burst allowance you propose (25% of committed tokens/day or the 2x rule) trigger automatic throttling or fail open? We prefer throttling over failing open — we want predictable behavior.

If you can draft the pilot quote reflecting a hard overage cap option (and one without the cap for comparison) we can route to procurement next week.

Alex
Director of Product, ClearWave
adunn@clearwave.ai | +1 (206) 555-4622

Subject: Fwd: Prod demo recap: pricing + burst 

Eve / Vivek — quick internal note on commercial levers we can use here before I sign any discounts into the HubSpot quote: 

- Offer an "elastic safety" add-on: first 25% of monthly committed tokens consumed as burst are billed at committed unit price (so effectively no overage for modest spikes).
- Tiered overage pricing: $1,000 / 1M tokens for consumption up to 2x committed in a billing period; $1,600 / 1M beyond that. (This is tighter than Evelyn's draft; gives finance a predictable marginal price.)
- Absolute overage cap: we can surface an optional spend cap at the invoice level (e.g., $12k/mo) but it requires explicit signature from procurement and a reconciliation process if exceeded — we typically move customers to an automated alert + soft-throttle first, then invoice if they elect to lift the cap.
- Promo: offer 30% usage credit in month 1 (to help them validate without risk).

I attached a quick draft pricing sheet (pricing-proposal-draft.pdf) to show math for 2M committed / burst patterns. Recommend we present two options in the quote: (A) lower committed price + modest burst allowance (B) slightly higher committed price + larger included burst and overage cap.

If Alex wants throttling behavior vs fail-open, choose soft-throttle (queue + 429) with immediate alert to engineering — better UX than a hard fail.

Ben
Director, GTM Pricing & Motion
ben_carter@redwood.com

Alex / team — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Quick update and next steps: 

1) Behavior on burst: we will configure soft-throttling (queue + 429) by default. We can enable a fail-open mode only with explicit finance sign-off and a hard overage cap.

2) Revised pilot options (we will send both quotes in DocuSign):
- Option A (predictability-first): committed 2M / month @ $930 / 1M; elastic safety: first 25% of burst billed at committed price; overage capped at $12k/month (requires PO signature).
- Option B (efficiency-first): committed 2M / month @ $860 / 1M; 25% elastic safety; overage tiers at $1,000 / 1M up to 2x committed; no hard cap (alerts + soft-throttling).

3) On procurement timeline: can the ClearWave procurement team confirm the preferred option and whether you need legal redlines? We can turn around a PO-ready DocuSign within 48 hours once you confirm.

4) Call: suggest a 30-min procurement sync Thursday 11/2 at 10am PT (I can send a calendar invite).

I'll publish both DocuSign options and the populated pricing workbook by EOD. If procurement wants an absolute cap, flag that and we'll include the reconciliation flow in the SOW.

Best,
